title: Kumai-218
dek: An ancient warforged whose trials join combat, judgment and teamwork across the earliest Pristinian training and the new vanguard’s formation.
imageAlt: Kumai-218 depicted as a warforged figure

facts.Known work: Keeps an arena and prepares fighters
facts.New company: The group that becomes the Veilguard

sources: Main quest-RP · selected primary scenes; anchors below
Supplied deep dossier · interpretation checked against quest evidence
body:
Kumai-218 is present long before the company that becomes the Veilguard. The quest record describes an ancient warforged who keeps an old arena, trains fighters and presses people to turn intentions into decisions. His severity can expose weakness, but it also creates friction with those he expects to teach.

March 2024 · the old arena

He welcomes fighters brought by Melian. He says he has made a long-lost gladiatorial colosseum his home and that Melian agreed to establish a settlement nearby. This is his account of their earlier connection, rather than an independently dated founding chronology.

Kumai explains that the arena’s magic prevents deaths and requires participants to face both one another and his constructs. The aim is adaptation under pressure. He recognizes Quake’s tactical precision, and the scene ends with Quake taking the contest.

John’s refusal to fight his companions challenges that method. Kumai calls him noble while questioning whether such restraint can survive war. He warns of betrayal but cannot answer away John’s commitment to sacrifice for others. The exchange preserves a disagreement about what preparedness should cost.

June 2025 · asking for a plan

During the Rahu crisis he calls the community together and insists that temporary success does not replace a strategy. He asks what they can offer, which risks they will accept and how they will keep fighting when powerful adventurers must leave.

His advice remains advice: he does not claim to know everything and tells the participants that they must convince one another. He describes his own responsibility as protecting the arena. In a later June exchange he also promises help defending the town while others are away. Neither act makes him Pristinia’s sole commander.

April 2026 · hearts before competence

Kumai asks Lady Severina, Pelagia, Thorn, Camilla Blackwood, Kasiri Ruza and Modeli to define leadership, honor and wisdom. He follows with hypothetical dilemmas involving loyalty, truth, sacrifice and victory. These are examination scenarios, not events the candidates actually carried out.

He then asks whom they would follow into battle. Support for Severina establishes peer trust, but does not finish the test. He returns in new armor with a sword and joins a free-for-all arena fight as another participant.

His automatons remove and revive him after he falls. Kasiri defeats Thorn at the end of the contest; Kumai praises her and tells the group to discuss their leader and report back. The outcome distinguishes martial success from final appointment. The earlier Vanguard remains a separate history from the new company.

May 2026 · results beyond the arena

He returns to the question of whether the trainees have acted on their lessons. A field test sends them after awakened undead and their leader. The choice to use that danger draws objections; his insistence that it is useful training remains his judgment.

When the group returns with the head, Severina credits Moira with uncovering the puzzle. Kumai’s sharp manner gives way to a brief acknowledgment of work well done. His standards include understanding a problem, rather than merely surviving a fight.

The open history

The meaning of his number, the full history of the arena and the extent of his formal institutional authority remain unresolved. He is not established as the Vanguard’s founder or sole membership authority. His teaching has a consistent concern with preparedness, while the people he teaches retain the right to disagree with its methods.
